summary: Yushu Batang Airport is a high-elevation regional airport situated on the eastern Tibetan Plateau in Qinghai Province, serving the Tibetan-majority Yushu Prefecture at approximately 3,890 meters above sea level. The airport was reconstructed and reopened in 2012 following extensive damage from the devastating 2010 Yushu earthquake, which leveled much of the surrounding town. It provides a vital lifeline for one of China's most remote regions, connecting local communities to Xining and other major cities.
faqs:
Q: How high is Yushu Batang Airport?
A: The airport sits at roughly 3,890 meters (12,760 feet) above sea level, making it one of the higher-elevation commercial airports in China. Travelers may experience mild altitude effects and are advised to stay hydrated.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Yushu?
A: The airport is primarily served by China Eastern Airlines and Tibet Airlines, offering regular connections mainly to Xining and occasional seasonal routes to other Chinese cities.

Q: When was the current airport rebuilt?
A: The modern airport was rebuilt after the catastrophic 7.1-magnitude Yushu earthquake in April 2010 and resumed operations in 2012 with improved infrastructure and seismic resilience.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, though winter operations can occasionally be affected by heavy snow, strong high-altitude winds, and low visibility. Travelers should monitor weather conditions during winter months.
transport_tips: The airport is located about 18 kilometers south of Yushu city center, with taxis being the primary means of ground transport; fares typically range from 60–100 RMB depending on your destination. There is no rail service to Yushu, so flying is by far the fastest option compared to the long, winding overland journey from Xining. Pre-arranging a vehicle through your hotel is recommended as taxi availability can be limited at peak arrival times.
local_tip: Pack a windproof jacket even in summer—temperatures at this elevation can drop sharply after sunset, and the plateau wind is significantly stronger than in lower-altitude parts of Qinghai. A simple portable oxygen canister can also be a lifesaver if you're arriving directly from lowland China.
